column2: IPF is restrictive: TLC, FVC and FEV1 fall together, so FEV1/FVC is normal or high (> 0.8); TLCO falls early.
The IPF hallmark is a UIP pattern: basal subpleural reticulation with honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis.
IPF causes V/Q mismatch with hyperventilation: low PaO2 with low PaCO2 (type 1 failure); hypercapnia is pre-terminal.
Antifibrotics (pirfenidone, nintedanib) halve FVC decline in IPF; prednisolone ± azathioprine increased mortality (PANTHER).
Velcro crackles, clubbing, restriction with low DLCO and a UIP pattern on HRCT is IPF once exposures and CTD are excluded.
Fibrosing alveolitis (IPF) gives fine late-inspiratory Velcro crackles and clubbing in up to half of patients.
IPF is a disease of older adults (60s–70s), rare before 50; onset at 30–40 should prompt a search for another cause.
Radiation pneumonitis 1–3 months after chest radiotherapy is treated with oral corticosteroids once infection is excluded.
Fixed obstruction (FEV1/FVC 0.50, no reversibility) in RA suggests obliterative bronchiolitis; methotrexate pneumonitis is restrictive.
With CT evidence of fibrotic ILD, full PFTs (spirometry, volumes, TLCO) confirm restriction and set a baseline before MDT review.
IPF gives tachypnoea, crackles, clubbing and cyanosis; tremor and hyperreflexia are unrelated neurological signs.
Subpleural reticulation with honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis on CT is a UIP pattern: IPF.
A typical UIP pattern on HRCT in the right context is sufficient to diagnose IPF after MDT discussion (ATS/ERS 2022); no biopsy needed.
FEV1/FVC 0.84 with normal volumes excludes obstruction and restriction; an isolated low TLCO needs Hb, HRCT and echo.
RB-ILD is a smoking-related ILD of current heavy smokers; smoking cessation is the key treatment.
Scadding stage IV sarcoidosis is established fibrosis, even if hilar nodes remain; stage I (BHL alone) usually resolves.
Recurrent pneumothorax with diffuse thin-walled cysts and a renal angiomyolipoma in a young woman is LAM; VEGF-D, sirolimus.
Progressive massive fibrosis (complicated CWP/silicosis) forms upper-zone conglomerate masses and can progress after exposure stops.
Silicosis is caused by respirable crystalline silica (quartz) in stonemasonry, quarrying and sandblasting.
IPF: all lung volumes fall (TLC, VC, RV) with a high FEV1/FVC and normal muscle strength (MIP).
HRCT pattern and distribution often give the specific ILD diagnosis without tissue and guide any biopsy.
Hypersensitivity pneumonitis from pet-shop birds: remove the antigen, with oral steroids for significant disease.
Silicosis increases risk of TB/NTM, fungal infection, lung cancer and autoimmune disease (RA, systemic sclerosis).
PMF follows coal or silica exposure; shipyard workers get asbestos-related disease.
Fever and breathlessness hours after mouldy hay is farmer's lung, from thermophilic actinomycetes (Saccharopolyspora).
The histological pattern of IPF is usual interstitial pneumonia: patchy, temporally heterogeneous fibrosis with fibroblastic foci.
Nintedanib 150 mg twice daily (or pirfenidone) slows FVC decline in IPF; prednisolone/azathioprine is harmful.
Eye involvement (uveitis) is the commonest clinical extrapulmonary site in sarcoidosis (25–50%); screen every patient.
Sarcoidosis is confirmed by non-caseating granulomas, usually from EBUS-guided lymph node sampling; ACE is non-specific.
Malt worker's lung is EAA from Aspergillus clavatus released when turning germinating barley.
Pleural plaques are benign markers of exposure and not compensable; asbestosis, diffuse thickening, mesothelioma and lung cancer are.
Opacities with a sharp straight edge following the radiation field 6 weeks after mediastinal radiotherapy are radiation pneumonitis.
Low VC and TLC with preserved peak flow, clubbing and crackles is a restrictive defect from pulmonary fibrosis.
Rock mining with upper-zone nodules and eggshell-calcified hilar nodes is silicosis; screen for TB.
Decades in building work with lower-lobe fibrosis, crackles and clubbing is asbestosis.
BHL with hepatosplenomegaly in a young Black woman suggests sarcoidosis; EBUS-TBNA plus transbronchial biopsy confirms granulomas.
Asbestosis is a fibrotic restriction with reduced TLCO (e.g. 45%); a raised KCO suggests extrapulmonary restriction.
Restriction (FVC 39%, ratio 96%) with clubbing and normal BNP suggests fibrotic ILD; HRCT confirms.
Upper-zone fibrosis in a pigeon keeper is chronic extrinsic allergic alveolitis; asbestos and drugs cause lower-zone disease.
Subacute flu-like illness with migratory opacities unresponsive to antibiotics is cryptogenic organising pneumonia; responds to steroids.
Erythema nodosum with BHL suggests sarcoidosis; serum ACE is raised in ~60%.
Löfgren syndrome (erythema nodosum, ankle arthritis, BHL) remits spontaneously in > 90% within 1–2 years.
Löfgren syndrome needs only monitoring and NSAIDs; steroids are for organ-threatening sarcoidosis.
Amiodarone causes lower-zone pneumonitis/fibrosis; silicosis, CWP, TB and ankylosing spondylitis cause upper-zone disease.
Basal-predominant subpleural reticulation on CT supports IPF; IPF reduces (not increases) TLCO.
Farmer's lung is caused by Saccharopolyspora rectivirgula in mouldy hay (type III/IV hypersensitivity).
Clubbing, crackles and basal subpleural honeycombing with negative precipitins is UIP/IPF; HP is upper/mid-zone with air trapping.
Uveitis with BHL in a young West African woman is sarcoidosis; a normal ACE does not exclude it.
